turns.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he would go to the door and call Estella, but he felt a bit nervous about it.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham told Pip to leave the room and return with Estella, her protégée, who would provide the boy with further instruction and company.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham told Pip to leave the room and return with Estella, her protégée, who would provide the boy with further instruction and company.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he would go to the door and call Estella, though he was quite apprehensive about meeting her.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham watched Pip with a mix of disdain and amusement, her eyes lingering on the boy’s nervousness. She told Pip, with a sharp edge to her voice, to fetch Estella immediately and ensure she understands that this is her duty and not a favor.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he would go to find Estella right away, though his heart was heavy with dread.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham watched as Pip scurried out of the room, his small form a stark contrast to the grandeur and decay of the chamber. She mused over the boy’s fear, her eyes narrowing as she considered the perfect vessel in which to pour her vengeance.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham watched the door through which Pip had disappeared, her gaze cold and calculating. She then called out sharply to a nearby servant, instructing them to ensure Estella was brought to her immediately.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip told the servant, who had appeared at Miss Havisham’s call, that he was to fetch Estella and remind her of her duty.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham watched the servant hurry off to carry out her instructions, her gaze lingering on the door Pip had left through. She then turned to a nearby clock, its hands frozen at the exact moment she had been betrayed, and with a bitter smile, she told the servant to inform Estella that she was expected to provide her usual entertainment for this unexpected visitor.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip thanked the servant politely for their help and turned to leave the chamber, his footsteps echoing off the walls as he made his way to find Estella.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham turned to the door Pip had just left through, her eyes narrowing as she considered her next move. She then called out to another servant, instructing them to ensure Pip was kept under her watchful eye and not allowed to leave the estate.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham watched the servant return with news of Pip’s whereabouts, her eyes narrowing with a mixture of curiosity and malice. She then told the servant to fetch Estella at once, her voice dripping with an icy command.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip who it was.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he was Pip, ma’am.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he was Pip?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip informed Miss Havisham that he was Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham told Pip to come nearer; let her look at him. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he was not afraid of a woman who had never seen the sun since he was born?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip replied that he was not.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he knew what she touched here?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he did, ma’am.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip what she touched?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that she touched her heart.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham exclaimed that it was broken!

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham told Pip that she was tired. She wanted diversion, and she had done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham said that she sometimes had sick fancies, and she had a sick fancy that she wanted to see some play. There, there! with an impatient movement of the fingers of her right hand; play, play, play!

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he was sullen and obstinate?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he was not, ma’am, he was very sorry for her, and very sorry he could not play just now. If she complained of him he would get into trouble with his sister, so he would do it if he could; but it was so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham remarked that it was so new to him, so old to her; so strange to him, so familiar to her; so melancholy to both of them! She asked Pip to call Estella.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham told Pip to call Estella. At the door.
